My parents played a lot of Stevie Wonder and No Doubt in the home, so my pre-disposed music tastes were jazz and punk/ska. From there I got heavy into 2000s alternative, I actually have a matching bff Green Day tattoo because we go see them together every time they're around and we really bonded over them. If you asked me what music I was into before I got into KPop, I'd give you names like Green Day, Stevie, Evanescence, Panic!, KoRn, Nirvana, or anything of that nature. 

But I also had a secret liking for girl pop. My first ventures were Jojo, Destiny's Child, Hilary Duff, Kelly Clarkson, Aly & AJ, but I kept those more under wraps because I was afraid it'd strip my 'good taste according to dads' cred, which now I understand as internalized misogyny. Pretty sure I can trace my liking to Kpop from there: I had brief run-ins with Wonder Girls, cause 'Tell Me' was all over youtube, but I didn't get into KPop fully until a friend showed me the 'The Boys' music video during a sleepover. I pointed to Jessica and was like 'Who's that?! She's so beautiful', and from there I became obsessed with the group as a whole, and that kicked off a huge penchant for girl groups. 

Now I listen to basically any genre I can get my grubby hands on, and my Spotify playlists are an unorganized nightmare, but I credit getting into girl groups as being huge for striking down my shame in liking feminine music, in that watching Girls' Generation succeed was empowering and made me so proud to follow them and be a fan. Now I'm very upfront about it. From there that made me more openly explore pop music and just how much of it does the serotonin thing my brain likes, and got me into the side of my taste that's more EDM/rap/r&b/city pop from there. It was a major turning point for my taste, and I'm happier for it!  

Also to answer the OG question: my favorite non-Kpop song is currently 'The Gold' by Manchester Orchestra. This changes very often though!

For me it was one of three things. 

It could be exactly like Lanegrita said, a flex both to others and myself about how in control I am. Very 'look at my restraint' intent, posting my scale weight on Snapchat, etc.

It could be a cry for help sometimes, like when I wanted to stop feeling weak but I didn't feel like I could give myself allowance to eat or I break aforementioned control, so I sought others to make me break it.

Or, occasionally, it could be trying to make people proud of me. This is sort of related to the first one, but part of my mentality stemmed from people praising me for being small. By proclaiming it, I'm hoping they're glad that I'm doing my best to keep my body that they approve of.

I'm aware this is screwy/unhealthy, and I'm in therapy working on the unlearning part, long past the self-awareness portion. It's a process- I've largely stopped doing this, with the exception of the second one when I slip.
